defects.field: operative_clauses[EO:10509#board].judgment_reason and first_end (cover-date route); dependent standstill first_end and whole_order_end
defects.claim_says: The letter of transmittal's date line in the held text, 'WASHINGTON, D. C., February 27,1964.', 'does not read cleanly as the corroborated date', so under D-20261125-board-cover-date the cover's 'FEBRUARY 17, 1954' dates the report
defects.source_says: The held text layer (source-ladder text, PDF page 2) reads cleanly as February 27, 1964: a legible day (27) and year (1964) that differ from the cover. D-20261125-board-cover-date applies only when the letter's date line is unreadable or not found; 'a letter date line that reads cleanly as another date is a conflict and stays an exception' (the Olney route likewise treats a differing legible month or day as a conflict). The rendered page image does show 'February 17, 1954', but the rule does not let a page-image reading convert a conflict into the cover route, and the claim's description of the line as not reading cleanly is inaccurate.

reasoning: The genuine claim restores 1954-02-17 (board) and 1954-03-19 (standstill and whole order); these agree with the cover, the page image of the letter and the claim's own arithmetic (1954-02-17 + 30 = 1954-03-19; exclusive 1954-03-18). Hashes, quotes, page labels (cover PDF page 1; stipulation PDF page 4), identity (EO 10509, Eisenhower, December 16, 1953), the two-clause inventory, the EO 12553 note and savings all check. It is rejected on the same ground I applied in the blind review: it uses the cover-date rule for a letter date line that the held text reads cleanly as a different day and year (February 27, 1964), which that rule makes a conflict and an exception. The historical date appears right on the page image; the defect is the route and its inaccurate description. A claim dated from the letter itself would need the board rule's held-text condition addressed, or an owner ruling on page-image corrections.
